evaluatr: Secure Independent Evaluation of Clinical Prediction Models

Source: R/evaluatr-package.R
evaluatr-package.Rd

The evaluatr package implements a two-component system for independent external validation of clinical prediction algorithms, designed to simultaneously satisfy:

  • Scientific rigour – fully independent evaluators with complete control over their data and reporting.

  • Commercial viability – model coefficients never leave the developer's private GitHub repository.

  • Data sovereignty – patient data never leaves the evaluator's secure local environment.

Workflow

  1. The model developer uses register_model() to create a protected model specification and registers the model with the evaluatr registry. The specification is uploaded to a private GitHub repository. The developer issues a time-limited, fine-grained access token to each evaluator.

  2. The evaluator calls secure_model_validation() with their local dataset and the developer-provided token. Predictions are computed entirely within the evaluator's R session; the output is a shuffled prediction-outcome matrix.

  3. The evaluator passes the result to eval_performance() to obtain discrimination, calibration, and utility metrics with optional bootstrap confidence intervals and diagnostic plots.

Security

Model coefficients are protected at rest and in transit; they are never exposed as readable R objects. Predictions are cleared from memory once returned. The returned matrix is row-shuffled so that predictions cannot be matched back to individual patient records. A minimum dataset size of 50 observations (per subgroup) is enforced to prevent near-individual prediction and coefficient reverse-engineering. Every validation event is logged by the evaluatr registry.

Example datasets

Three example datasets are included with the package:

  • dvt_example – simulated DVT diagnosis dataset, 9,805 patients across seven studies (binary outcome). Loaded via read.csv(system.file("extdata", "dvt_example.csv", package = "evaluatr")).

  • bc_survival_example – breast cancer relapse-free survival dataset, 2,232 patients with a pre-assigned development/validation split (survival outcome). Loaded via read.csv(system.file("extdata", "bc_survival_example.csv", package = "evaluatr")).

  • adnex_sample – de-identified ADNEX ovarian cancer validation dataset, 1,500 patients (multinomial outcome). Loaded via readRDS(system.file("extdata", "adnex_sample.rds", package = "evaluatr")).
